question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose plugin-emitted AI-safety events and durable operator queries as a core public contract, and if so what privacy, retention, authorization, and compatibility guarantees should that contract make?
rationale: This PR adds public plugin and Gateway surfaces plus durable state; source review can assess mechanics, but only maintainers can choose whether those long-lived product and security semantics belong in core.

options.title: Approve a narrow core contract
options.body: Define the supported event families, trusted observer model, retention bounds, authorization scope, and SDK compatibility promise, then require the PR to implement and document exactly that scope.

options.title: Keep the event bus internal
options.body: Retain only internal diagnostics hooks and move exporter, UI, or plugin-facing safety workflows to the plugin ecosystem until a narrower core API is sponsored.

options.title: Split the proposal
options.body: Land a reviewed internal telemetry foundation separately and defer persistent history, plugin emission, and UI/Gateway queries until their product contracts are individually approved.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow core contract
recommendation.body: Define the supported event families, trusted observer model, retention bounds, authorization scope, and SDK compatibility promise, then require the PR to implement and document exactly that scope.

likelyOwner.reason: A current-main owner could not be established from the supplied history artifacts, so this needs routing through the diagnostics/plugin ownership path.
